analysis.title: ISM Services Index Fell in October, But Remained in Expansion
key_insights: The ISM Services Index fell to 54.5 in October from 54.9 in September, staying comfortably in expansion (above 50). It has been in the mid-50s since late 2025, after falling to around 50 in mid-2025 when tariffs were much higher, and has held there even with the conflict with Iran.
All four subindices used to compute the headline were above 50 in October. Business activity and new orders fell over the month, while employment and supplier deliveries rose.
The employment subindex rose to 51.4, its highest level since February, but is still only modestly expansionary. PNC notes employment has been stronger in 2026.
The prices subindex was 73.0 in October, down from 74.0 in September. October was the second highest reading since June 2022, after September. PNC says inflationary pressures remain intense.
Of the six subindices not used in the headline, four rose and two declined, and all indicated expansion.
Fifteen of the eighteen industries reported expansion. Growth was strongest in transportation and warehousing, wholesale trade, information, and retail trade.

Construction and health care contracted. PNC calls this somewhat surprising given data center construction and health care's share of job growth (more than half of private sector job growth over the past year). It suggests weak homebuilding and federal spending cuts as possible causes.

Survey respondent comments were generally negative even though the economy is solid, with Q3 annualized real GDP growth of 3.4%. Respondents cited high energy prices and tariffs as drags, while some noted strong demand.

ISM manufacturing rose one point in October to 55.5. Together with services, PNC reads the two indices as pointing to solid growth at the end of 2026, with the economy continuing to expand into 2027. High energy costs and tariffs remain drags, and reduced optimism about tech is the main downside risk.

Midday on 4 November the S&P 500 was up almost 2% after Democrats won majorities in both the House and the Senate, by a larger margin than markets expected. PNC says markets are pricing continued growth and perhaps reduced uncertainty given likely gridlock over the next two years.

The 10-year Treasury yield was down 7 basis points to 4.91% and WTI crude was down more than 8% to around $88. PNC presumes the oil move reflects expectations for a quick end to the U.S. conflict with Iran now that Democrats control Congress. The dollar was slightly weaker.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Down from 54.9 in September but comfortably in expansion, consistent with solid services growth.
Highest since February but only modestly expansionary.
Down from 74.0 in September but second highest since June 2022, signalling intense inflationary pressure.
Prior-month reading, the highest since June 2022.
Up one point from September and in expansion.
Economy remains solid despite negative survey comments.
Down 7 basis points on the day as markets priced in gridlock and continued growth.

risk_factors: Reduced optimism about tech is a major downside risk to the economic outlook.
High energy costs and tariffs remain drags on growth.
Elevated services prices (prices index 73.0) point to continued inflationary pressure.
Weak homebuilding and federal government spending cuts may be weighing on construction and health care.
geopolitical: Conflict between the U.S. and Iran. PNC says the ISM services index has stayed in the mid-50s despite it.
WTI fell more than 8% on 4 November, presumably on expectations of a quick end to the U.S. conflict with Iran now that Democrats control Congress.
Democrats gained majorities in both the House and the Senate in the congressional elections, and PNC expects gridlock over the next two years.
